  (prec is the precision class the row is ranked in, and the only set of options it is ever
   ordered against: a lane that computes in single precision is not a faster answer to the
   double lane's question, it is an answer to a different one, so no column here is read
   across precisions. ns/arg is the reference lane's own lower-quartile cost scaled by this
   option's ratio to it at the middle of the run's rounds — a central ratio and not the
   lower quartile of the same ratios, because the reference's ratio to itself is one in
   every round and any quantile of it is one, so a lower quartile there would credit the
   reference with the middle of its rounds and score every other option below the middle of
   its own — a credit for whichever row the run anchored on, and worth more than the
   margin between the fastest options. hi is the same scaled by the upper quartile of those
   ratios, lo the same scaled by their lower quartile; both are formed inside a round and carry
   no drift common to one, and spread is hi over lo — the ratio between the two ends of that
   row's own band, a factor and not a cost. 'vs ref band' is the range the option's ratio to
   the reference lane fell in
   over the run's rounds, at its lower and upper quartiles, and
   drift% is how far that ratio moved between the run's first and second half — a pair whose
   ratio drifts does not carry a decaying clock alike, and the confidence line below says
   whether any pair drifted further than this run can order. 'peak ns' is the single fastest
   round the option was seen in; it bounds what the option can do at a peak clock and is
   never the option's cost, because under a decaying clock the fastest round is the
   earliest one, which a caller with a long workload does not meet. The verdict column is the
   accuracy one, against the bound in the row's own bound column: 'within bound' met it,
   'within the floor' is above its own bound but at or below the certified lane's 5.5e-14,
   which this comparison cannot separate, and 'ABOVE BOUND' means the option did not deliver
   what its own lane documents.
   Every bound in the column is read from the library, and every one of them applies over
   every argument the row was measured on: the certified lane's own figure for the certified
   rows, and the figure the library documents for the entry
   the row reaches for the narrower lanes and for the partitions — naming a partition changes
   which fitted tables that entry reads, not the entry's own figure. A partition also publishes
   a figure of its own, for its stored fits over the interval those fits cover and for nothing
   outside it, and that figure is not the row's judgement: the measured column is a difference
   from the certified lane rather than an error against the true function, and past the fitted
   interval the entry is running the certified lane's own arithmetic. A row reading a partition
   therefore names that figure and the interval it holds on beside its verdict, and the column
   stays the entry's whole-domain figure. The measured column itself is the worst difference
   over the arguments this run sampled, so it moves with --xrange and --count: a figure from
   one range is not comparable with one from another, while the verdict is, because the figure
   it is judged against does not move. The verdict does not wait on a pass:
   the values a lane returns are a property of the build, so a run on a machine whose
   clock wandered still reports which rows delivered what they document, and its cost
   columns read 'not measured' only where no figure could be formed at all.)

the far region's representations — what answers an argument at or above kX1, one member
  per row, swept from the library's own table of the axis and called over this run's far
  arguments. They are not cells of the space below: the entry that takes a member takes no
  route, so no cell of this shape could run it, and the axis is measured here instead — once,
  untimed, and ranking nothing. The figures are relative, where the measured column above is
  absolute: F_n falls to 2.6e-14 at kX1 for n = 32, so an absolute figure over the whole
  domain would be the fitted regions' error and would not move for any change here.

the accuracy classes — one precision and one question shape, the only sets this
  probe orders inside
  A class is the set of options that are alternatives for one need a caller has: one precision
  (fp64, fp32, fp16 or bf16), built at the library's full-accuracy multiplier, and one question
  shape — what the
  option hands back. The five shapes here are, in the seam's own order:
    single      one call per order per argument: F_n(x) for one order at one argument
    all-orders  one argument per call: F_0(x)..F_n(x) at that argument's own order n
    fixed-n     one call per order over the array: F_n(x_i) at one fixed order n
    all-n       one call per order run: F_0(x)..F_nmax(x) for every argument of the array
    all-n-at-orders  one call over the array: F_0(x_i)..F_n[i](x_i) at each argument's own top order
  The shape is part of the key for the reason the precision is: it changes what
  the caller gets back, and the figure below is per argument, so ranking an option that returns
  one argument's ladder against one that returns a whole array's would rank the amount of output
  against the arithmetic. Everything a caller does not choose — the fit route, the evaluation
  scheme, the partition of the fitted regions, the packing axis, the division form the recursion
  ends in, and the exponential a region-B ladder is seeded with — is a way of computing the same
  answer and is a column inside the class, so those options compete in one ranking rather than
  dividing it. The seventh axis a policy carries, the budget the lane's engine runs at, is not a
  column: it is a property of the lane, so it is part of the class's key by way of the precision,
  and every cell of one class runs at that one budget. Membership is decided by the precision and
  the shape, never by comparing one lane's
  documented figure against another's — a figure belongs to one lane, and reading it across lanes
  is how a class ends up empty by construction. Every row of a class was built at the same
  multiplier and answers the same question, so nothing inside it traded accuracy for speed and
  nothing inside it answers something else: the entry each class names is its fastest option at
  the library's full accuracy, for that question, on this machine and no more. Nothing here is ordered
  across classes: another precision or another shape is an answer to a different
  question, not a slower answer to this one.

              precision showed over the 60 paired rounds was 28.88%. It is measured in the
              paired ratios, which is the quantity the ordering is made of, and not in
              absolute times: every pair's band is formed inside a round and the
              ordering is made pair by pair from that pair's own band, so this number states
              how coarse the class's own measurement got and bars nothing. The
              canary's widest pass spread beside it was 74.70% — context, and not the
              bar: a clock that decays widens a fixed work read by wall clock and
              cancels in a ratio, which is why the two columns differ and why the
              second is the one the ordering uses.

  this ranking is this machine's: a different host, a different compiler or a different set of
  build flags can rank these options differently, which is why the probe is run where the numbers
  are used rather than read from documentation. A figure above is the option's within-round
  ratio to the reference lane at the middle of the run's rounds, scaled by that lane's own cost:
  a paired reading, so no clock drift common to a round is in it, and a central one, so it
  does not credit whichever row the run anchored on. Its spread is printed beside it, and the
  peak column bounds what each option can do at a peak clock and is never the option's cost.
  The resolution above is this run's: a steadier machine would order pairs this one could not.

not measured by this probe, by design — listed so that nothing above is read as a complete
  account of the library:
  * the native half lane (region C only, orders 0..8, results scaled by a power of two — a
    different question from this workload's);
  * the region-A matrix-product transform (region A alone, so measuring it means composing the
    rest of an evaluation, and the composition would be what got measured);
  * the CUDA lanes (a separate optional build, and a lane this probe reaches with no arm at
    all: `benchmarks/boys_option_probe.cpp` names no CUDA entry and this probe calls
    none, so a row of that lane would be a host entry's figures under a device name);
  * a partition's stored fits read directly: the figure a partition row prints beside its
    verdict is the library's published figure for that partition's fits, and every row above
    is an entry read end to end, so nothing here measures a fit's own error against the true
    function over the interval it is cut for — the library's accuracy gate measures that book;
  * the call shapes other than this workload's all-orders-per-argument one, which the seven axes
    are not crossed with. Every other shape the seam's key names is measured at its class's
    own default policy alone - one row per class, and no crossing of the axes - so the
    all-N grouping and its sorted-argument overload, the fixed-order call that returns one
    order across an array, the array entry that reads a per-argument order, and the
    single-order call at each format the library declares it for are all measured above.
    Those rows are no cell of the space, and they are counted in the closure below,
    which names them and counts the crossing they stand for: 0 row(s),
    standing for the 0 cell(s) of their own class that crossing them
    with the axes would add beyond the cells they stand at.
    Crossing them with the axes is outstanding work and not an impossibility: an entry is a
    function, and no table of entries exists in this library for one to be counted from. A
    class the seam's key reaches that this run produced no figure for is named in the
    build-defaults block above, with the reason this run has for it. What the closure
    does count is every row this report carries and the cells it stands for. The axes are
    crossed on every precision class: the routes each class's own lane reports its fits
    in, the schemes, partitions, packing axes and division forms of that lane and the
    exponentials its region-B ladders can be seeded with, one row per served cell of a
    class this machine can run.
